svg.text: coding_agent — LangGraph Assessment Pipeline
A state machine (a flowchart the code actually walks through, step by step) with 7 steps, saved to disk after every step, run in a loop up to max_planner_steps=8 times per CLI call
CLI: coding-agent generate --md file.md
cli.py → Settings.load() → Orchestrator → graph.invoke() × max_loops
1. build_context
MdSummaryAgent (LLM, cheap tier) →
MdParserAgent (rule-based, NO LLM) →
SkillEntry[] + CoverageMatrix + SkillGraph
plain: reads the lesson file, writes down the list of things it teaches
graph/nodes.py:build_context — this is where skills are pulled out of the .md file
2. retrieve_context
ContextRetrievalAgent (RAG — looks up past examples)
SkillTriageAgent (LLM, cheap tier): 1 call →
picks skill order + how many TYPE_A/B/C + sim_package_id
Wires the tool list onto the generator
plain: decides what to ask for next and what "flavor" each question is
TYPE_A = pure math/Python bug · TYPE_B = ROS2 node, wrong string · TYPE_C = math bug inside a node
3. generate
QuestionGeneratorAgent (LLM, primary model)
3-part reply: JSON spec / starter code / reference code
Prompt is built from (in order):
• real check examples from evaluations/test cases/
• few-shot examples from past approved runs (memory.py)
• feedback from the previous rejected attempt, if this is a retry
Tool calling happens here — see purple box on the right
plain: the AI actually writes the question + code + fix
agents/question_generator.py — several questions written in parallel (ThreadPoolExecutor)
4. validate
DifficultyCalibrationAgent (LLM, cheap tier, batched)
OriginalityAgent (math similarity check, no LLM)
SupervisorAgent.compare_to_eval_bank() — eval calibration #1
compares to evaluations/question.json+solution.json
(text-similarity match → is the difficulty label about right?)
ConfidenceScoringAgent._rate_test_case_quality() — eval calibration #2
1 LLM call, batched, compares to evaluations/test cases/
(rates the grading checks 0-100 → test_case_quality score)
PlannerAgent.evaluate_quality() → pass/fail per question
plain: checks the work; good ones are kept, bad ones go back for a redo
passing → accumulated_questions · failing → stays for regeneration
planner.decide()
REGENERATE / NEXT_BATCH
/ FINALIZE
plain: what do we do next?
NEXT_BATCH = still more questions to write → back to generate
5. reflect
PlannerAgent.reflect() — 1 LLM call that critiques the failure
writes feedback text for the failing question(s)
plain: explains what went wrong so the retry can fix it
feedback goes verbatim into the next regenerate prompt
6. regenerate
QuestionGeneratorAgent.regenerate()
ONLY the failing questions are replaced, using the feedback
Same tool calling as step 3
plain: rewrites just the bad questions, not the whole batch
up to max_regeneration_attempts=2 tries per question slot
regenerate → back to validate (re-checked)
7. supervise
SupervisorAgent.validate() — final check over the WHOLE batch
coverage ≥ target, at least 1 approved, validation_score ≥ 75
optional second-opinion LLM judge (enable_llm_judge)
plain: is this whole batch good enough to ship?
score = 0.6×eval_score + 40×pass_rate → APPROVED / REJECTED
export_run_v2()
outputs/<run>/questions/Q*/{question.yaml, solution.yaml,
README.md, ros_ws/(5-file grading harness)}, reports/*.json
plain: writes the finished files to disk
REJECTED + loops left?
→ prompt (or --yes) → another CLI loop → build_context again
plain: if it failed and we still have tries left, start over
Tool calling — the AI can ask for extra info mid-answer
Set up in retrieve_context, used from inside generate/regenerate (steps 3 & 6) via llm.complete_with_tools()
plain: "tool calling" = the AI pauses, asks a real function for data, then keeps writing using that answer
fetch_ros2_docs
Context7 API — looks up real ROS2 docs
plain: required before writing medium/hard ROS2 code
search_course_exercises
Tavily/Exa web search
plain: finds similar real-world exercises for grounding
fetch_course_content
Fetches one specific web page
plain: reads a URL the AI wants more detail on
check_similarity
Compares against past questions stored locally
plain: catches near-duplicate questions
query_skill_graph
Looks up which skills depend on which
plain: checks prerequisites and coverage
estimate_difficulty
Quick local formula on the code, no LLM
plain: a self-check before submitting
submit_question
The AI's way of handing back its final structured answer instead of plain text
plain: "I'm done, here's my answer in the exact shape you asked for"
Skill extraction (step 1 — build_context)
plain: reading the lesson and making a list of "things a student needs to know"
MdSummaryAgent
LLM, cheap tier — shortens the .md file
plain: makes a summary, cached so it's not redone
MdParserAgent
plain rules/code, NO LLM call
plain: splits the summary into a skill list
→ CoverageMatrix (skill → has a question tested it yet?) + SkillGraph (which skill needs which)
→ SkillTriageAgent (step 2, LLM) then picks the TYPE_A/B/C mix + order + sim_package_id
TYPE_A: pure Python/math bug, no rclpy · TYPE_B: ROS2 node, one/two wrong strings
TYPE_C: math bug inside a node's callback (e.g. wrong field or formula)
Eval calibration — two separate comparisons (step 4 — validate)
plain: "how does this question compare to real, human-made examples?"
#1 SupervisorAgent.compare_to_eval_bank()
Compares against: evaluations/question.json + solution.json (titles/scenarios/skills)
Method: text-similarity match, no LLM call — finds the closest real questions
Feeds: half (10 of 20 points) of the difficulty_eval_calibration score
plain: "is this question's difficulty label believable, compared to real ones?"
#2 ConfidenceScoringAgent._rate_test_case_quality()
Compares against: evaluations/test cases/ (real grading scripts) via eval_bank_criteria.py
Method: 1 batched LLM call rating the grading checks 0-100
Feeds: the full test_case_quality score (20 points)
plain: "would this actually catch a wrong answer, or is it a rubber stamp?"
Framework
plain: the whole pipeline is one flowchart the code walks, with a save point after every box
LangGraph StateGraph (graph/builder.py) — 7 steps bound via make_nodes(orch)
Branching after `validate` decided by PlannerAgent.decide() — plain code, not an LLM call
Saved with a SqliteSaver checkpointer — every step is written to disk, so --resume RUN_ID works
State passed between steps as plain dictionaries (validated Pydantic models at each boundary)
graph.invoke() runs once per CLI loop; max_planner_steps=8 caps ticks inside one invoke call
Confidence score (0-100 per question) — 5 buckets, 20 points each
plain: how the pipeline decides "is this question good enough to ship?" — set in config/config.yaml confidence_weights
coverage (20)
does this question actually test
a real skill from the lesson?
plain: on-topic check
difficulty_eval_calibration (20)
10: declared vs. re-checked difficulty
10: eval calibration #1 (question bank match)
plain: is the difficulty label honest?
originality (20)
1 minus how similar it is to
questions already generated
plain: not a copy-paste repeat
format_quality (20)
all the required fields are
present and filled in
plain: nothing is missing/broken
test_case_quality (20)
eval calibration #2 — LLM rating
of the grading checks' realism
plain: would the test actually catch a wrong answer?
Pass bar: min_confidence_score (50 by default) AND no hard blockers (out of scope / not auto-gradable / near-duplicate) → APPROVED
